chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, what you did for Yunus has pleased me. He said to me: Is it not part of what Allah did for Yunus that He transferred him from Iraq to the vicinity of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)?

key_terms.يُونُسَ: Yunus (specifically Yunus ibn Ya'qub in this context)

ai.seo_question: What divine favor did Allah grant Yunus ibn Ya'qub regarding his proximity to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elevates Yunus ibn Ya'qub, a prominent companion and supervisor of the Imamate's affairs, by linking his physical relocation from Iraq to the vicinity of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) as a divine reward for his service. This narration underscores the Shia concept of *qurb* (proximity) to the Ahl al-Bayt as a spiritual merit, suggesting that Yunus's burial site or status was honored through this connection to the Prophet. It reflects the scholarly view that the companions' loyalty to the Imams is intrinsically tied to their connection with the Prophet, thereby validating their high status in the afterlife.
